topic.name: Properties of the Unit Circle in the First Quadrant

question.text: The point $P\left( \dfrac{6}{7},\dfrac{\sqrt {13}}{7}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\tan\theta?$
question.explanation:
Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta$ as follows:

\[ x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta \]

We're given that $x=\dfrac{6}{7}$ and $y=\dfrac{\sqrt {13}}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

\[ \cos\theta = \dfrac{6}{7}, \qquad \sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{7}. \]

Knowing that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos\theta},$ we can calculate $\tan\theta:$ \[ \tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt {13}}{7}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{6}{7}\right)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{6}. \]

question.text: The point $P\left( \dfrac{ \sqrt{11}}{6},\dfrac {5}{6}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\csc\theta?$ Do not round your answer.
question.explanation:
Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta$ as follows: \[ x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta \]

We're given that $y=\dfrac{5}{6}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have \[ \sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{6}. \]

Knowing that $\csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta},$ we can calculate $\csc\theta:$ \[ \csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{ 5}{6}\right)} = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{6}{5}} \]

question.text: The point $P\left( \dfrac{2}{3},\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\tan\theta?$ Do not round your answer.
question.explanation:
Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta$ as follows: \[ x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta \]

We're given that $x=\dfrac{2}{3}$ and $y=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have \[ \cos\theta =\dfrac{2}{3}, \qquad \sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}. \]

Knowing that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos\theta},$ we can calculate $\tan\theta:$ \[ \tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)} = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}} \]
